newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee sellers hold back for higher prices.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee sellers hold back for higher prices.

text.p: Vietnam's robusta coffee market dried up this week as farmers held back stock in the hope of getting higher prices later, traders said on Friday.

"It's been quiet for the last few days, everyone's in a state of shock because prices have dropped," said one trader. "Now they are not willing to sell at these prices because they have seen higher prices before."
Buyers were said to be bidding at around $1,330 a tonne, FOB Saigon Port, but no trading was going on.
"At that price no one wants to sell, it's just a bid price from the buyers," said one trader, noting that bids had been as high as $1,480 earlier this month.
Traders said some 200,000 tonnes of coffee had so far been sold from the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) crop, which they estimated at about 270,000-280,000 tonnes.
"So maybe there's 70,000 to 80,000 tonnes left. If we get an uptrend in the futures market, people will be eager to sell again," said one trader.
However, he said that although there had been a slight bounce on the New York market on Thursday, the trend remained unclear.
